investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads — 2 nodes report insufficient VM resource quota and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract is fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~142–144 seconds before the probe timed out. No VM was provisioned, so the eval runner could not populate any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract validation failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an eval runner bug or a code regression.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), so the effective schedulable pool is already limited to 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any quota exhaustion on those nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads — 2 nodes report insufficient VM resource quota and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract is fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~142–144 seconds before the probe timed out. No VM was provisioned, so the eval runner could not populate any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract validation failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an eval runner bug or a code regression.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, confirming slots are held by non-preemptable pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), so the effective schedulable pool is already limited to 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any quota exhaustion on those nodes.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads simultaneously request kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, the 2-node pool may be structurally too small to absorb peak demand, causing recurring scheduling failures.

UNLIKELY — Eval runner misconfiguration or token/auth failure: the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1882 would return SKIP (not fail) if args.token were missing, and the failure message is a Kubernetes scheduler event, not an API auth error. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-14 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource both reported insufficient VM quota, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~142–144 seconds across all three checks before the eval timeout fired. Because the agent VM was never started, the probe in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918, createAgent call) never returned an agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected, causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 266–270) to fail completely.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes configured with this resource have no remaining VM slots, so any new remote-agent pod is immediately Unschedulable. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules changed or nodes were relabeled, the effective capacity would shrink even if per-node VM quota is unchanged.

TERTIARY — concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods consuming all VM slots: a prior eval run, a user-initiated agent, or a pod that failed to clean up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

QUATERNARY — cluster scaling or node failure: one or more kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have become NotReady or been removed, reducing total VM capacity below the level needed to schedule even a single new pod.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed ample remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on both eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause would not be resource exhaustion and an alternative (e.g., API-level rejection, network partition, or auth failure) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling race or a briefly-held lock rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.
If the node affinity/selector on the pod matched more than 2 nodes, the 4-node exclusion would not be a contributing factor and the diagnosis would focus solely on per-node VM quota.
If leaked or stuck pods were not found holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the cause would shift toward absolute capacity limits (too few VM slots provisioned) rather than a cleanup failure.

If only one of the three sibling checks had failed with this message (rather than all three), a shared cluster-level cause would be less likely and a per-check configuration issue would need to be considered.
